title: Light Differentiable Logic Gate Networks
claim: Our reparametrization cuts compute, memory and training cost relative to the original while keeping or improving accuracy.
layout: 1 panel, grouped bars per metric, left-to-right, values labeled above bars
description: A single grouped bar chart with a legend at the top: blue for Original and orange for Reparametrized. The y-axis is 'Relative Scale (per metric)' from 0 to 1.2. Five metric groups run left to right: Forward pass, Backward pass, Training steps, Model size and Test acc. In each group the Original bar is normalized to 1.0, and the raw value is printed above it, for example 222000 steps and 625.0 model size. The orange bars are shorter for forward pass (about 0.92), backward pass (about 0.54), training steps (about 0.12) and model size (about 0.25). Test accuracy is the exception: the orange bar is taller, at 29.3% against 27.2%. Black error bars sit on the timing bars. The eye goes first to the large drops in the orange bars.
caption: For a CIFAR-10 DLGN [ref], our reparametrized DLGNs require 4x less memory, converge in 8.5x fewer training steps, and perform the forward and backward passes in up to 8% and 45% less time, respectively. Details in [ref] and Appendix [ref].
abstract: Differentiable logic gate networks (DLGNs) exhibit extraordinary efficiency at inference while sustaining competitive accuracy. But vanishing gradients, discretization errors, and high training cost impede scaling these networks. Even with dedicated parameter initialization schemes from subsequent works, increasing depth still harms accuracy. We show that the root cause of these issues lies in the underlying parametrization of logic gate neurons themselves. To overcome this issue, we propose a reparametrization that also shrinks the parameter size logarithmically in the number of inputs per gate. For binary inputs, this already reduces the model size by 4x, speeds up the backward pass by up to 1.86x, and converges in 8.5x fewer training steps. On top of that, we show that the accuracy on CIFAR-100 remains stable and sometimes superior to the original parametrization.
